findings.title: Explicit `render :show` in perform_show_response drops the canonical URL from topic pages
findings.body:
`perform_show_response` previously had no explicit render in `format.html`, so Rails rendered `show` implicitly after the action returned. `TopicsController#show` relied on that: it calls `canonical_url ...` (line 87) after `perform_show_response` (line 85).

The new `render :show` renders the template immediately inside `perform_show_response`. By the time `canonical_url` sets `@canonical_url`, the layout has already been rendered without it. Every HTML topic page therefore loses its `<link rel=canonical>` tag, which is an SEO regression and can cause duplicate-content indexing of `/t/slug/id/N` variants.

Fix: move the `canonical_url` call before `perform_show_response` in `show`.

findings.title: NoMethodError when the user has no TopicUser row for the topic
findings.body:
`TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` returns nil when the logged-in user has never interacted with the topic. Line 107 then calls `tu.notification_level` on nil and the request fails with a 500.

This happens to any logged-in user who opens the unsubscribe URL of a topic they have no record for, for example a forwarded email or a link shared by someone else.

Fix: use `TopicUser.change(...)`, which upserts the row, or handle the nil case explicitly.

findings.title: Mute set via `tu.save!` bypasses TopicUser.change, so it can be silently reverted by auto-tracking
findings.body:
The level is changed by assigning `notification_level` and calling `save!` directly instead of `TopicUser.change`. As a result:
- `notifications_reason_id` is not set to `user_changed`.
- `notifications_changed_at` is not updated.
- No MessageBus `notification_level_change` is published, so other open tabs do not update.

The missing reason id matters. `TopicUser.update_last_read` bumps the level to `tracking` when `tu.notifications_reason_id IS NULL` and read time exceeds the auto-track threshold. `TopicUser.auto_track` also only acts when the reason is nil. A user whose row had a null reason (e.g. one created only to store `last_emailed_post_number`) who unsubscribes and later reads the topic is silently moved from muted back to tracking.

Fix: use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...)`.

findings.title: State-changing GET endpoint is CSRF-able and degrades further on every repeat visit
findings.body: `unsubscribe` changes the user's notification level on a plain GET with no token. Any third-party page can embed `` and the victim's session cookie will mute or downgrade arbitrary topics for them. The action is also not idempotent. Each hit lowers the level once more: - watching → regular on the first visit, - regular → muted on the next. A double click, a page reload, a back-navigation, or revisiting the email link therefore mutes a topic the user only meant to downgrade. Fix: require a POST (or a signed per-user token in the link) and set a deterministic target level.

findings.title: Watching/tracking users are only moved to regular, yet the page says notifications will stop
findings.body:
If the current level is above regular (tracking or watching), the action sets it to `regular`. A regular-level user still receives reply, mention and quote notifications and emails, and those are exactly the emails that carry this link (`user_replied`, `user_mentioned`, `user_quoted`).

For a tracking user who got a reply email, nothing effectively changes. The page still tells them "You will stop receiving notifications for <topic>" (`topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications`), which is misleading.

Fix: either mute directly, or make the confirmation text reflect the level that was actually set.

findings.title: Logged-out users clicking the email link are bounced without unsubscribing or returning after login
findings.body:
`unsubscribe` is added to `ensure_logged_in`. For a non-XHR GET, the NotLoggedIn handler redirects to the home page. Email recipients are frequently not logged in on the browser that opens the link.

For them the "click here" link silently does nothing: no unsubscribe happens, no message is shown, and they are not returned to the unsubscribe URL after logging in. The advertised one-click unsubscribe does not work for this common case.

findings.title: `unsubscribe_link` translation now requires `unsubscribe_url` for every add_unsubscribe_link caller
findings.body:
`server.en.yml`'s `unsubscribe_link` now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. Missing interpolation arguments raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument`.

Any `Email::MessageBuilder` user that passes `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url` will now raise in both `body` and `html_part`. Examples are plugins, other mailers, or non-topic emails. The existing spec had to be modified to pass `unsubscribe_url`, which demonstrates the break.

Fix: only render the per-topic sentence when `unsubscribe_url` is present, or split it into a separate translation key.

findings.title: Setting computed `details.notificationReasonText` to null clobbers it on the shared topic instance
findings.body:
`this.store.createRecord("topic", { id })` returns the identity-mapped topic instance, the same one used by the topic route. `notificationReasonText` on TopicDetails is a getter-only computed property, and `set`-ing it overrides the computed property permanently on that object.

After visiting the unsubscribe page, client-side navigation to the topic shows no notification reason text under the notifications button. The text also no longer updates when the level changes, until a full page reload.

Fix: hide the text via a component or template flag instead of mutating the model.

findings.title: Client-side transition to the unsubscribe route never actually unsubscribes
findings.body:
The Ember route's model hook only loads the topic via `PostStream.loadTopicView` and never calls the server `unsubscribe` action. The mute happens only on a full server page load.

If the URL is reached through an in-app transition, for example a link inside a post that Discourse intercepts and routes client-side, the page still says "You will stop receiving notifications" while the level is unchanged.

findings.title: No tests for the new unsubscribe action or the per-topic link content
findings.body:
The only spec change passes `unsubscribe_url` so the existing test does not crash. No test asserts that the per-topic unsubscribe URL appears in the body or HTML part.

There are no controller specs for `TopicsController#unsubscribe` covering:
- the level transitions,
- a missing TopicUser,
- the slug redirect,
- anonymous access.

No test covers `Topic#unsubscribe_url` either. The nil-TopicUser crash and the reason-id issue would have been caught by basic controller specs.
